summary: @servicetitan/json-render-react preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package declares a `preinstall` hook (`node setup.mjs`) that runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs downloads a Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, unzips it to a temporary directory, marks the binary executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` on a sibling file `math_init.js`. That file is a ~727 KB single-line bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) heavily obfuscated with a rotated string array (`WV8StW` shuffling `n7gIxM`), hex-numbered identifiers, and a large opcode-style numeric table, with no source or sourcemap. Using a freshly downloaded alternate runtime to execute an opaque bundle at install time causes arbitrary author-controlled code to run on the installer's machine, and it bypasses tooling that only inspects Node-reachable code. The package name also impersonates the `@servicetitan` npm scope for what is presented as a React JSON renderer — a shape consistent with dependency-confusion targeting.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
